transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Mark Dawson (HelioThera - Procurement), Elena Ruiz (HelioThera - CISO), Tom Briggs (HelioThera - Platform), Sarah Patel (HelioThera - Legal)

Summary:
Quick alignment on legal open points (MSA/DPA), SLA thresholds, KMS/escrow language, and a microbenchmark plan to validate latency/cost tradeoffs for a near-term pilot. Agreed owners and dates for redlines and benchmarks.

Topics:
- MSA redline priorities: KMS, audit logs, termination/escrow
- DPA comments and data residency
- SLA targets and remedies (p99 latency, uptime)
- Pricing paths: hosted vs dedicated vs dedicated-reserved
- Technical preflight: network egress, VPC peering, KV cache behavior
- Next steps and deadlines

Action items called out in meeting (also in metadata above).

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood - AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, well keep this tight, 50 minutes on the calendar. quick roll call?
[00:08] Mark (HelioThera - Procurement): Mark here, Elena, Tom and Sarah are on as well.
[00:12] Elena (HelioThera - CISO): Hi all.
[00:14] Tom (HelioThera - Platform): Tom here.
[00:16] Sarah (HelioThera - Legal): Hi team.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood - SE): Great thanks. Quick agenda: legal redlines, SLA thresholds, and then a short technical preflight so priya can call out benchmarking well run.
[00:30] Mark: Sounds good. For procurement we need to make sure the MSA covers the typical stuff but two big asks: in-country data residency for EU customers and stronger audit log retention. Also pricing approval needs an example cost run.
[00:45] Alex: Yep, thats fair. On the MSA weve flagged the KMS language and the egress fee table as priority. We can supply a redline focused on those two items.
[00:55] Sarah: To be explicit: were fine with standard SOC 2 type stuff, but we need the option to bring the key on-prem (HSM) or a customer-managed KMS. Can Redwood support customer-managed KMS integrations?
[01:10] Priya: Short answer yes — we support external KMS via standard KMS integrations, and we can provide a path for HSM key wrapping. But the operational model is different if you choose customer KMS, so well write that into the redline. note: sometimes transcription shows K M S as V P C etc.
[01:28] Elena: Okay good. Also, how do you surface audit logs and retention periods? We need immutable audit trails for two years.
[01:36] Alex: We have per-tenant audit logs and can set retention tiers. By default hosted keeps 90 days but enterprise plans can extend. Well propose 2 year retention in the MSA addendum for Dedicated or Private deployments.
[01:50] Sarah: What about exportability? We need logs exported to our SIEM with guaranteed delivery.
[01:56] Priya: Thats supported; we offer streaming to customer endpoints (syslog/S3) and can provide delivery SLAs as part of the addendum. well include the connector spec in the doc we send.
[02:10] Tom: On the technical side: we need to validate p99 for generation under our 1kb prompt distribution. Were sensitive to tail latency, and we were also hoping to quantify cost per 1k tokens with and without KV cache priming.
[02:25] Priya: Great. We propose a microbenchmark: 1 hour run, your sample traffic replay, measure p50/p95/p99, and cost delta with prefix cache warm vs cold. Well also include a small experiment on batching thresholds.
[02:40] Mark: timeline? procurement needs something to approve pricing - ideally a realistic cost projection for a pilot (roughly 100k tokens/day).
[02:50] Alex: Priya and Tom will do the microbenchmark during week of May 11. Priya will deliver a cost sensitivity table by May 15. Ill send the MSA redline by May 13.
[03:02] Sarah: For the DPA: we have a few special clauses around subprocessors and a request for 3rd party subprocessor list and 30-day notice before new ones. Can you provide that?
[03:14] Alex: Yep we have a subprocessors list and we can commit to notice. DPA redlines are normal for enterprise. well attach our standard DPA and highlight subprocessor flow.
[03:24] Elena: Also, is there an escrow option? We have procurement rules that for certain vendors we need code/ML-model escrow or at least clear runbook.
[03:33] Alex: We dont typically escrow models but we can discuss escrow for critical pieces — often customers choose a combination of documented runbooks + operational SLAs. We can put proposed escrow language in the MSA as an optional schedule.
[03:46] Sarah: Okay please include proposed wording.
[03:49] Tom: Networking question: we plan to use VPC peering for Private deployment. Does Redwood support V P C peering and dedicated egress IPs for allowlisting?
[03:58] Priya: Yes we support VPC peering and static egress IPs in Private/Dedicated modes. Note: for hosted, we support VPC connector but not full peering. Sometimes the transcript says V P C peering as V P C peering or VPC peer, sorry about the stutter.
[04:15] Tom: Good — well need the IP ranges and egress SLA to update our firewall rules.
[04:20] Alex: Well include the egress ranges in the technical appendix. Also, egress fees are called out in pricing; we can show a table of typical egress for your pilot.
[04:30] Mark: Pricing: procurement wants two options — hosted pay-as-you-go with a per-token price, and a reserved dedicated pool option with monthly commit. Can you show break-even points?
[04:42] Priya: Yes, well produce a breakeven chart in the microbenchmark artifacts — typical crossover depends on throughput and prompt length, but for sustained 100k tokens/day we often recommend dedicated reserved.
[04:56] Mark: Competitors — finance asked whether Redwood has anything unique vs VaultCloud.
[05:00] Alex: High-level: our differentiation is predictable economics + unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and a more opinionated operational model (cache, batching) to control cost. But we will avoid marketing language in the MSA.
[05:12] Elena: For risk: what are SLAs and remedies? We need p99 latency SLO of 500ms for lookups and p99 generation target of sub-5s for 1k tokens. Also uptime SLA and credits schedule.
[05:28] Priya: We can commit to a mapped SLA in Dedicated with specific p99 and uptimes; hosted has best-effort numbers. Remedies typically are credits, and for enterprise we can negotiate stronger remedies. Well include proposed numbers in the SLA schedule.
[05:45] Sarah: On termination and data return: we need guaranteed deletion, data export within 30 days, and certificates of destruction.
[05:53] Alex: Agreed — standard schedule includes data return + deletion certification. For Private deployments some of these are customer-managed.
[06:02] Mark: Any blockers for procurement to approve a pilot?
[06:06] Sarah: From legal, the remaining items are: KMS language clarified, DPA subprocessors clause, escrow wording, and audit log retention/export guarantee.
[06:16] Alex: Right — well focus redline on those. Priya will run the microbenchmark with Tom and deliver cost numbers.
[06:24] Tom: Ill share the sample traffic dump and PII classification by Tuesday May 12. note: the file is ~120MB so well use a secure share.
[06:34] Priya: Perfect — make sure the traffic includes your typical prompt lengths and p95 token sizes. well run warm and cold cache tests.
[06:43] Mark: procurement would like to see a simple run-of-cost for 30-day pilot with both hosted and dedicated numbers.
[06:50] Alex: That will be included in Priyas deliverable and Ill summarize in the MSA email.
[06:55] Sarah: One process note: we prefer consolidated redlines instead of piecemeal. Please send a single packet with MSA+DPA+SLA redlines and a short readme.
[07:05] Alex: Will do — consolidated packet by May 13.
[07:08] Priya: Any final technical asks?
[07:10] Tom: Just that the benchmark includes an experiment with prefix KV cache warm-up and shows delta. Also include quantization variant notes if possible.
[07:20] Priya: Well include quantization guidance for cost/perf tradeoffs in the artifact. sometimes the transcript will mis-hear quantization as quanti-sation or quanta-thing.
[07:31] Alex: Alright lets recap. Next steps: Alex sends consolidated MSA/DPA redline by 2026-05-13. Priya runs microbenchmark with Tom the week of 2026-05-11 and delivers artifacts + cost table by 2026-05-15. Sarah consolidates legal open points and returns DPA comments by 2026-05-14. Tom provides traffic and PII classification by 2026-05-12.
[07:56] Mark: That timeline works for procurement gating.
[07:59] Elena: Thanks, looking forward to the artifacts.
[08:02] Alex: Thanks all. Ill follow up with a calendar invite for the hands-on microbenchmark session and upload the redline packet. Links shared: MSA redline (will upload), technical appendix draft: https://redwood.ai/docs/helio-poc (placeholder), subprocessors list link: https://redwood.ai/security/subprocessors (placeholder).
[08:20] Sarah: Thanks everyone.
[08:22] (call ends)

Meeting recap (short):
- Primary blockers: KMS customer-managed options, audit log retention/export, DPA subprocessors language, escrow wording.
- Agreed microbenchmark and timeline to generate cost comparison.
- Owners assigned and deliverable dates set.
